chose: A rate-limited lane parks: the claude-code adapter reports a stream `rate_limit_event` whose status is `rejected` on SessionExit.rate_limit {type?, resets_at?}. On a lanes run that launch never counts as a stall; its lane takes no task until the reset the stream names (+30s), or for 5 minutes doubling to 60 per consecutive park when none is named, and the task goes back to the queue for other lanes. A session that registered before the limit still files its handoff. With every lane parked the run waits for the earliest reset, still honouring --stop and ^C. A serial run is unchanged (a limited launch still stalls).
over: Stopping the run on a rate limit; parking every lane on one lane's limit; parking a serial run too; matching stderr prose
because: M1: a usage-limited launch looks like an unresolved stall and two stop the run, though nothing is wrong with the work. The stream names the limit and its reset, so the wait is read from a fact, not guessed. Routes can send lanes to different agents, so one lane's limit is not assumed to be every lane's. The serial run's behaviour is pinned byte for byte by 2.2.
